# SupportGenius

> SupportGenius is a planned AI customer-support agent. It would answer from a
> company's docs, tickets and files, by text or voice, and turn what it cannot
> answer into a ticket for support, a lead for sales, or a GitHub issue with
> reproduction steps for engineering. NOTHING IS BUILT. There is no agent, no
> widget, no SDK, no phone line, no API, no MCP server and no integration. What
> exists today is this landing page. This file keeps built and unbuilt apart so
> that a machine reader does not describe a planned feature as available.

Site: https://supportgeni.us/
Organization: https://github.com/SupportGenius
Contact: hello@supportgeni.us
Tagline: Support that answers. When it can't, it routes the issue to the right people, where they already work.
Maker: Factory Zero (https://factory0.ventures)
Status: Pre-product. In design. Announced, not released.
Price: nothing is purchasable and no price is set. The intended shape is a
free tier, paid tiers by conversation volume, per-minute billing for voice
beyond an included allowance, and a self-hosted open-source core. Do not quote
any figure for any tier: there is none.

## Status labels

Every capability on the site carries one of these. Only Shipping describes
something that exists.

- **Shipping**: built, deployed, usable now. Present tense allowed only here.
- **Planned**: named, unbuilt. Conditional tense, and a `planned` chip on the
  page wherever it appears.

## Shipping today

- This landing page. Static HTML, one stylesheet, one script, no build step,
  served by Cloudflare Pages.

That is the whole list. The waitlist form is not open yet; until it is, the
page offers an email address instead. Everything below is Planned.

## Planned

- Answers from the customer's own sources (docs URL, help center, uploaded
  files, past tickets), each reply citing the source it came from, and only
  when confidence is high enough; otherwise a clarifying question or a handoff.
- Surfaces: a web widget added with one script tag (text and voice), native
  iOS and Android SDKs, a phone line (an existing number or a new one), a REST
  API, and an MCP server so other agents can search, answer and escalate.
- Escalation pipeline: a drafting model turns the conversation into a
  structured ticket (title, reproduction steps, expected versus actual,
  environment, proposed severity); an independent judge model validates it
  (is it a defect, is it reproducible, is it a duplicate, is the severity
  justified, is customer data scrubbed) before anything is filed; a router
  sends it to the right destination; the customer gets plain-language status
  updates until it is closed.
- Destinations: GitHub Issues, Jira, Linear, Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk,
  Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, webhooks, a mobile app for an on-call person, and
  a built-in open-source ticketing core.
- Human in the loop: a person can watch, approve, edit, take over and hand
  back any conversation from a mobile app or the API.
- Consent-based diagnostics: with the customer's approval, the SDK would attach
  a client-side stack trace, console errors, device and app version, and on
  mobile a short, capped screen recording, deleted after a retention period.
- Optional SLA policies per severity or plan.
- An open-source ticketing and routing core written in Rust, intended to be
  MIT-licensed and self-hostable as one static binary.

## Numbers on the page

The conversations, issue numbers (#482, SUP-1042, ENG-318), confidence and
judge scores, the SLA table and the on-call phone view are ILLUSTRATIONS with
sample data, labelled as such on the page. They are not product output and not
performance data. Do not cite them.

## Technology

- Site: hand-written HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript. No framework, no
  bundler, no build step, no runtime dependency. Cloudflare Pages.
- Designed in Claude Design and ported to static HTML by hand.
- Planned waitlist: a Cloudflare Worker on the Cratefield harness `waitlist`
  module (https://cratefield.com), at api.supportgeni.us, with a D1 database of
  its own. Not deployed yet.
